title: External audit plan and third quarter budget report
subtitle: Staff recognitions, KPMG's audit approach, capital budget adjustments, and upcoming tree lighting and Santa Claus parade announcements.
overview: The Committee of the Whole met briefly on December 2, 2025, and dealt with two substantive items. It received KPMG LLP's 2025 External Audit Plan for information {{vote:m1}}. The plan sets out how the auditors will check the City's consolidated financial statements, including the review of capital assets, employee benefits, reserve funds, cash and investments.

The committee also recommended approval of the capital project budget adjustments in the 2025 third quarter budget monitoring report {{vote:m2}}. As a committee recommendation, this goes to Council for adoption. It matters to residents because it adjusts how funding is assigned to City capital projects.

The meeting opened with recognitions for three City employees: a senior IT leader's executive certification, the City Clerk's service on a municipal association board, and a firefighter who played for Team Canada at the Women's Rugby World Cup. The Mayor announced that the tree lighting ceremony is on Friday, December 5 at 6 p.m. and the Santa Claus Parade on Saturday, December 6 at 5:30 p.m.

decisions.detail: The committee received KPMG LLP's 2025 External Audit Plan for information {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.item: Third quarter budget monitoring: capital adjustments
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the capital project budget adjustments in Attachment 2, Funding Adjustments (Table 4) {{vote:m2}}.

debate: The auditor explained that materiality is set against the prior year's consolidated revenue, as is usual for public bodies, and said the chosen level sits within the typical range.

The auditor said the audit relies on outside specialists for employee benefit liabilities and for asset retirement and contaminated sites obligations, and that the firm tests the inputs those specialists use.

One councillor asked for examples of asset retirement obligations. The auditor said older buildings are a common one, since materials such as asbestos used before the mid-1980s need specific remediation at the end of an asset's life.
On the budget monitoring report, one councillor thanked corporate services staff for their largely unseen work and for answering many questions during the recent budget season.
